title: How many passwords can a six letter lock have?
description: Laksh wants a lock with six slots of letters, thinking it is safer than a five digit lock. The video multiplies the choices slot by slot, compares the two locks and counts six digit pincodes, and Keeko doubts how six slots of twenty six combine.
teaching_notes: One idea: when every slot has the same number of choices, the passwords are that number multiplied by itself once for each slot. Watch for students who multiply twenty six by six instead of using six slots of twenty six.

source: How many passwords does a lock with 6 slots of letters A to Z have? Compare it with a 5-digit lock, and say how many 6-digit pincodes are possible.
video_script.why: A learner sees that a slot with twenty six choices multiplies the passwords by twenty six, and sees why the letter lock is safer than the digit lock.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lock with six letter slots, the five digit lock for comparison, and six digit pincodes
video_script.anchor: Laksh with the new lock of six letter slots
video_script.wrong_answer: one hundred and fifty six passwords
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies twenty six by six instead of using twenty six six times
video_script.payoff_line: A six letter lock has twenty six to the power six passwords

final_answer.value: 26 to the power 6, which is 308915776 passwords; up to 1000000 pincodes
final_answer.spoken: twenty six to the power six, which is thirty crore eighty nine lakh fifteen thousand seven hundred and seventy six passwords; up to ten lakh pincodes

names.Laksh: plans to buy a lock with six letter slots because it feels safer

maths_rules: each slot has 26 choices: 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 = 26^6
video_script.design: One idea: slot choices multiply, once for each slot. Wrong idea: twenty six times six. The six slots build by pairs of slots and the large total only appears at the answer.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; Laksh with a new lock of six slots, each slot showing a letter from A to Z

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='lock'/>Laksh plans to buy a lock with six slots. Each slot takes a letter from eigh to zed.
<bookmark mark='safe'/>Laksh feels this lock is safer than the five digit lock.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many passwords are possible with such a lock?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one slot with the 26 letters; for each letter of the first slot, 26 letters branch from the second slot

marks.slot: one slot turns through the 26 letters
marks.next: each letter of the first slot grows 26 branches for the second slot
marks.same: the same idea as the ten choices of the digit lock is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='slot'/>The letters from eigh to zed are twenty six, so every slot has twenty six choices.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Under each letter of the first slot, the second slot again has twenty six choices.
<bookmark mark='same'/>It works like the digit lock, but every slot now has twenty six choices and not ten.

marks.given: six slots are drawn, each marked with 26 letters

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a lock with six slots, and each slot has twenty six letters to choose from.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of passwords, compared with the five digit lock, and the six digit pincodes

marks.find: the words number of passwords, compare, six digit pincodes are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the passwords, compare them with the five digit lock, and count six digit pincodes.

beats.on_screen: 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 = 26^6, one 26 for each slot

marks.each: a 26 is written under each of the six slots
marks.power: 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 x 26 = 26^6 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='each'/>Step one, write the choices for each slot. Every one of the six slots has twenty six.
<bookmark mark='power'/>The passwords are twenty six multiplied six times. We write that as twenty six to the power six.

beats.on_screen: 26 x 26 = 676; 676 x 676 = 456976 for four slots; 456976 x 676 for six slots

marks.six: 456976 x 676 is written for six slots, the result is left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, multiply in pairs of slots. Twenty six times twenty six gives six hundred and seventy six.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Six hundred and seventy six times itself covers four slots.
<bookmark mark='six'/>That is four lakh fifty six thousand nine hundred and seventy six. Two more slots multiply by six hundred and seventy six once more.

beats.on_screen: a pincode has 6 digit slots: 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 = 10^6

marks.pin: six digit slots are drawn for a pincode, each with 10 digits
marks.ten: 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 = 10^6 appears, the result is left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='pin'/>Step three, look at a six digit pincode. Each of the six slots has ten digits.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>The pincodes are ten multiplied six times. That is ten to the power six.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 26^6 = 308915776 passwords; 10^6 = 1000000 pincodes; 308915776 is more than 3000 times 100000

marks.cmp: 308915776 is set beside 100000, more than 3000 times larger

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>A six letter lock has twenty six to the power six passwords.
<bookmark mark='num'/>That is thirty crore eighty nine lakh fifteen thousand seven hundred and seventy six.
<bookmark mark='cmp'/>The five digit lock has only one lakh. The letter lock has more than three thousand times as many.
<bookmark mark='pin'/>Six digit pincodes can be as many as ten lakh.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 26 x 6 = 156, struck out; 26 x 26 = 676 for just two slots beside it

marks.fix: 26 x 26 = 676 for two slots appears beside the bubble
marks.all: the bubble is struck out and six 26s are written multiplied

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the lock has one hundred and fifty six passwords, from twenty six times six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But two slots alone already give six hundred and seventy six passwords. Six slots must give far more.
<bookmark mark='all'/>The six tells us how many times twenty six is multiplied, not what we multiply by.
